 Judgment

The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in RTA.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioner case are that, on 28-11- 2022 at about 7.30a.m., he was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03/KH-9894 on Bangalore to Kolar NH-75, near Lanco Toll,
Hoskote Town, Bangalore Rural District, at that time, the driver of the Trailer Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-32/K-1666 drove the same, in a very rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came at high speed, suddenly took 'U' turn without giving any signal and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident, due to forced impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and the duty doctors examined him clinically and radiologically, which revealed that petitioner had sustained severe head injury (SAH with Acute SDH), Left sided haemothorax, he underwent surgeries and treated with conservatively for which he will require huge funds for treatment, medicines etc., and accordingly, the petitioner is still under treatment and he was forced to spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food,
transport and other charges.

Due to said injuries he completely bed ridden, cannot run, jump, stand,
cannot lift or carry any weight and unable to sleep property, he cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and he undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering, permanent in nature.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 41 years, he was coolie work and earning Rs.1,000/- per day.
Due to accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work and he lost the earnings and suffering from mental shock and mental agony.

4. It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-32/K-1666, against the said lorry Hoskote Police have registered the Cri.No.418/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 338 of the IPC.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner under all heads.
5. In pursuance to the notice, respondent No.1 has appeared before the Court through its counsel filed its written statement.

Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Tribunal, hence he has Jagadeesh vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110435421/
2 placed as exparte.

sentences.text: 6. Brief averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 are that, the petition is bad in law for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties as the insurer and insured of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 03/KH-9894 are not made as parties.
The police authorities have not investigated the matter as required U/Sec.158(6) of MV Act r/w Rule 231(1) of MV Rules.

It is further contended that the rider/petitioner of the motorcycle was not having valid driving licence he has not following any traffic rules and regulations himself only caused the accident and sustained injuries and without proper investigation the jurisdictional police and petitioner colluding with each other have falsely implicate the insured Lorry and filed a false complaint and create false story to claim wrongful gain against this respondent.
Respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
It is further respondent No.1 has denied the accident, age, income, injuries and also income of the petitioner.
It is further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and prays to dismissal of the petition.

7. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 28-11-2022 at about 7.30a.m. he was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 03/KH-9894.

Proceeding on Bangalore- Kolar NH-75 road, when reached near Lanco Toll, Hoskote Town, Bangalore Rural Dist., at that time, driver of one Trailer bearing Reg.No.TN-32/K-1666 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came at high speed without giving any signal, suddenly took 'U' turn and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?

8. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked the 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 14 and the petitioner got examined the MRO of Siliconcity Hospital,
Bangalore as PW.2 and got marked the 04 documents as per Ex.P.15 to 18.
The petitioner got examined the Dr. Sreedhara K.C. as PW.3 and got marked the 03 documents as Ex.P.19 to 21.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any witnesses and not produced any documents before the Tribunal.

9. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials available on record.

For the following reasons, this Tribunal has given answer to the above Issues as under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming the compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
12. The petitioner is examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 documents.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R. Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.8 is the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.9 is the copy of reply to the Notice, Ex.P.10 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.11 is the medical bills, Ex.P.12 is the medical prescriptions, Ex.P.13 is the copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, Ex.P.14 is the copy of D.L.
In cross examination, he has stated that, the lorry was suddenly turned to take the U turn.
Further denied that the accident took place due to his negligence.
He get conscious after one week after the accident.
The people present at the accident place were informed about the vehicle.

13. Another witness Sri. Mahesha B. who is the Medical Record Officer at Siliconcity Hospital,
Hosakote is examined as PW.2 and he has produced 04 documents marked as Ex.P.15 to 18.
Ex.P.15 is the authorization letter, Ex.P.16 is the copy of MLC, Ex.P.17 is the police intimation and Ex.P.18 is the Inpatient Records.

14. The petitioner got examined the Doctor by name Dr.Sreedhara K.C. who is the consultant Neuro Physician & Rehabilitation/Mental Health and MLC Consultant at Deepashri Hospital and Neuro Rehabilitation Center and Previously at NIMHANS as PW.3.

Further denied that he has given higher disability.
15. The respondents have not adduced any evidence and not produced any documents.
16. Respondent No.1 has contained that, there is a delay of two days in filing the complainant.
The offending vehicle is not involved in the case and it has been falsely implicated in this case.

On perusal of Ex.P.16, the MLC report, it appears that, it has been entered on 28.11.2022 at 8.20 A.M.
by the Siliconcity Hospital and history is road traffic accident.
On perusal of Ex.P.17, it appear that police intimation has been issued on 28.11.2022.
On perusal of Ex.P.5 the IMV report, it appears that the rear right side brake light and indicator assembly of the offending lorry was damaged.
On perusal of these documents, it appears that, the MLC was issued on same day of the accident and the offending vehicle has sustained the damages on its rear right side.
The petitioner was also unconscious for 7 days.

Therefore it appears that, the delay in filing FIR is properly explained and Jagadeesh vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110435421/

As per sketch, spot mahazar and charge sheet, it appears that, on the date of accident, the driver of offending vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, suddenly took 'U' turn without giving any signals and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
As a result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Hence, the Hosakote Police have filed charge sheet against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 of IPC r/w Sec.121 and 177 of IMV Act.
18.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

sentences.text: 19. The respondent No.1 took contention that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.1 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.1 has not proved that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
20. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1 the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 the copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 the copy of IMV Report
, Ex .
P.6 the wound certificate,

Ex.P.7 the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.8 the copy of 133 notice, Ex.P.9 the copy of reply to the notice, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Trailer Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-32/K-1666.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced wound certificate issued by Siliconcity Hospital, Hosakote and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents have not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the wound certificate, it is discloses that the petitioner has sustained CLW over left eye and Head injury (SAH with Acute SDH), the doctor opined that the injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.

Therefore,
taking all these facts and nature of injury, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
22. The petitioner produced medical bills for Rs.2,06,626/-, which is marked as Ex.P.11.
The respondents not denied the said medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.2,06,626/- under the head of medical expenditure.
23. The petitioner not produced any documents with respect to expenditure of transportation, food and other charges.

However, the petitioner has produced the discharge summary of Siliconcity Jagadeesh vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110435421/
5 Hospital, Hosakote at Ex.P.10 and PW.2 has produced the inpatient records of petitioner, wherein it is held that the discharge summary to show that he has treated as an inpatient.

sentences.text: It discloses that, the petitioner took treatment inpatient in the said hospital from 28-11-2022 to 09-12-2022 i.e., for about 12 days.

Therefore, considering the treatment taken as inpatient in the hospital, this tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.12,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and conveyance charges.
24. The petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Dr. Sreedhara K.C. as PW-3.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.3 deposed that, he has examined the petitioner on 20-02- 2025 at Deepashri Hospital and Neuro Rehabilitation Center, patient is complaining of severe headache,
giddiness, on and off loss of memory, disturbed, blurred vision and is oriented to time place and person, social interaction poor, social interaction poor, communication poor, judgment slightly impaired, presently not working.

entities.text: Deepashri Hospital and Neuro Rehabilitation Center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: CT scan brain done at spectrum on the same day, dilatation of ventricular system and prominence of sulcal spaces noted involving both cerebral hemispheres- Suggestive of age related parenchymal atrophic changes.
Irregular gliotic area is noted involving right temporal lobe with associated ex-vaco dilatation of temporal horn of right lateral ventricle sequelae to previous insult.

Further he referred to Neuro Psychological Assessment for which the report of said assessment reveals that Severe impairment of motor speed, focused attention,
category of fluency, working memory, response inhibition, learning verbal memory, verbal comprehension, visuospacial construction.

Suggestive of Pre frontal cortex, bilateral dorsolateral,
temporal lobe, frontal lobeinvolvement and advised cognitive retaining and neuro psychological profile suggestive of Cognitive disability.

As per recent examination report and photo copy of disability assessment manual and neuro psychological report and also CT scan film and report the petitioner has got disabilities of self-care-mild deterioration in self-care, interpersonal activity friction on isolated occasions, nervous or irritable, communication and understanding- social anxiery and work-liability to work and he assessed mild disability 40% and the whole body disability is 26.6%.
In the Cross examination admitted that, personally he had not treated the petitioner and further denied that the petitioner has taken followup.
However by considering the nature of the wounds, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the petitioner at 20% to the whole body.

25. The petitioner stated that, at the time of accident he was aged about 41 years and he was doing coolie work, he used to earn a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot do any work as earlier.
The petitioner had not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
The accident is of the year 2022.
In present days the coolie worker get Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.
However, by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/-.
26. As per Ex.P.13 and 14 Notarized Copy of Adhar Card and driving licence, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01-01-1981 and 08-05-1974 respectively.
In the discharge summary the age of the petitioner is shown as 47 years.
Therefore, age of the petitioner is taken as 48 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 13 which comes as follows:

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal awards Rs.4,83,600/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
27. The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medical expenses for further treatment.
In the chief-examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, he is forced to spent huge amount for future medication.
PW.3 the Doctor has not stated anything about the requirement of future or followup treatment.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioner required future treatment and estimation for the same.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

28. The petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was working as coolie and earning Rs.1,000/-
per day and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to attend the work and facing financial difficulties.
The petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 28-11- 2022 to 09-12-2022.

Therefore, by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.
29. The petitioner sustained grievous injury as shown in the wound certificate.
The petitioner was doing coolie work and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

30. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount  1. Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
 2.

Medical expenses Rs. 2,06,626/-
 3. Transportation, 12,000/-
 Nourishment, Conveyance Rs.
 and attendant charges.
 4. Loss of future income on 4,83,600/-
 account of Permanent  disability  5. Towards future medical Rs. NIL  expenses  6. Loss of income during laidup Rs. 30,000/-
 period.

7. Towards loss of amenities of Rs. 30,000/-
 life  Total Rs. 8,12,226/-

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,12,226/-, which is rounded off to Rs.8,12,250/-.
31. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
32. Liability:-
As already observed above, Respondent No.1 being the insurer and Respondent No.2 being the owner of the Trailer Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-32/K-1666.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driving of the offending vehicle, hence respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, the respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
33. Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.8,12,250/- with interest @6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner (As the petitioner has incurred huge amount towards medical expenses) with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
19. The respondent No.1 took contention that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.1 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.1 has not proved that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore,
taking all these facts and nature of injury, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.2,06,626/- under the head of medical expenditure.
The petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 28-11- 2022 to 09-12-2022.
Therefore, by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.
In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.
Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driving of the offending vehicle, hence respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
